newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise says no decision on Suez div.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise says no decision on Suez div.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux chairman Jerome Monod said on Thursday that no decision had been taken about an exceptional Cie de Suez dividend.
Cie de Suez shareholders, including Saint-Gobain, have asked for a special dividend before any merger that would reflect Suez's capital gains and profit potential.
"It is not up to me to speak for Suez," Monod told Reuters after a news conference. "But I can say that the board of Suez has not yet decided on the size of their (1996) dividend.

"It is the prerogative of the Suez board to decide the amount but it is clear that the final amount will impact the terms of the merger. If there is 100 and they pay 10 then there remains 90," Monod said.
"The boards have agreed the principle of a merger. Detailed operational and financial talks about this plan are now starting and we have to wait for the outcome," he said.

Earlier, during the news conference, Monod declined to react directly to newspaper reports over a "special" Suez dividend of at least three billion francs aimed at winning over the approval of Suez stake holders.
He said that any such financial details had not yet been discussed, let alone decided, between the boards of the two companies and he added that all board members had signed a confidentiality clause.
Lyonnaise and Suez will hold special board meetings on April 11 to detail the merger.
A Lyonnaise official said that it was likely there would be news conference on April 14.
